exposure: maternal age (<20 years, 20-24 years, 25-29 years, 30-34 years, and >=35 years)
cohort: The study included 94,410 Japanese women with singleton pregnancies from the Japan Environment and Children's Study.
finding: Both advanced maternal age (>=35 years) and teenage pregnancy (<20 years) were associated with an increased risk of placental abruption compared to maternal age 20-24 years.
